vision_features.abnormalities:
1. White-to-pale-grey powdery coating: Present across the upper surfaces of the majority of leaves throughout the entire plant canopy. The coating is diffuse and uniform in distribution, covering both the central lamina and areas near the veins. It gives the leaf surface a dusty, flour-like, matte-white appearance. The coating ranges from light dusting to heavy, dense coverage that nearly obscures the underlying green leaf color. Affected leaves appear pale grey-green to almost white overall. No distinct border or margin — the coating blends gradually. Texture appears dry and superficial, like a fine powder sitting on the surface.
2. Leaf distortion and curling: Many leaves throughout the canopy show upward cupping, puckering, and edge-curling or crinkling. This is most pronounced in the upper, younger portions of the plant. The distortion is irregular and affects leaves of various sizes.
3. Pale green to whitish coloration of the entire leaf surface: Leaves that are heavily coated appear to have lost normal deep green coloration across the entire blade. The interveinal areas appear lighter green to pale cream-white, while veins may retain slightly more green.
4. A single leaf held by the hand at lower left is severely coated — the entire upper surface is covered with a dense white powdery layer, almost completely masking the underlying tissue. Size is approximately medium (5–8 cm across). Shape of the mark follows the entire leaf surface diffusely.
5. Lower leaves and petioles near the base show some pale, slightly yellowish-green discoloration with lighter streaking.
vision_features.absences: 1. No visible water-soaked, dark brown, or black dead tissue patches are apparent on the leaves. 2. No visible raised pustules, thread-like growths, or orange/brown/rust-colored structures are present. 3. No obvious wilting or stem collapse is visible — stems appear structurally intact. 4. No visible insect bodies, webbing, or sticky exudate is apparent on the leaf surfaces.
vision_features.summary: The plant is extensively covered with a dry, white-to-pale-grey powdery coating that blankets the upper surfaces of nearly all leaves throughout the canopy, giving the whole plant a dusty, washed-out appearance. The coating is most dense on upper and mid-canopy leaves, with some leaves almost entirely white. In addition to the surface coating, many leaves show physical distortion including upward cupping and crinkling, particularly in younger growth at the top. The leaf held in the foreground most dramatically illustrates the heavy, uniform white powdery coverage. The leaf surfaces are the most severely affected organ, and the single most striking feature is the dense, uniform, dry white powdery coating covering virtually every leaf on the plant.
